# EXPLORATORY / POST HOC: how far the host prices overstate host time (28 Nov 2026)

**EXPLORATORY / POST HOC. Nothing is scored or rescored; no host price is changed; BUNGA is not refitted; nothing new is measured.** H1 stays P2 0.1183, P4 0.2495. Generated by `scripts/null_kernel_bias.py`; numbers in `null_kernel_bias.json`. Intervals: percentile bootstrap at the lock's settings, resampling whole cells (or layers for S4).

**The mechanism is the per-layer idle-gap residual, not null-kernel bias.** The committed prices do not read the null pass, and nothing here is a finding about TaxBreak's method, which uses its null kernel only for a constant launch floor.

Two instruments, kept apart. The **null pass** is this study's own extension of a null kernel to every launching call, under the tape's and null device's Python modes; it is banked as a comparison. The **committed price**, which P2's and P4's predictions read, is the bare timer's per-call price plus the per-layer idle-gap residual (ruling of 1 Nov 2026). Priced / measured is a **lower bound** on priced / true host time: the host issues every operation before the timer stops.

## S4 (L4, 1 Nov 2026): null pass against the recording run

One cell (dense 1 L1951 b1 (L4); the only S4 cell whose recording trace is banked). Null pass over the recording's layer span, over 28 layers: 1.78 [1.72, 1.86]. Whole prefill: null pass 134.2 ms against the recording's host time 77.4 ms (1.73x). The recording is profiled, so this too is a lower bound.
